assessments.reasoning: Section 1.1 in Report 490 directly describes SETL2 as evolved from SETL. Its contrast of scoping, procedure values and unsupported SETL features bounds the relationship.

challenge.method: Read the opening and comparison bullets together. Checked whether the passage addressed code ancestry or the language design and whether it named the acquired Dewar copy as an exact edition parent.
challenge.results: The direct evolutionary attribution supports language-design lineage. The report cites the 1986 SETL book for background and leaves code genealogy, edition equivalence and general substitutability unestablished.

limitations: The target is the SETL language identity. Keep implementation history and exact parent-manifestation claims separate.
